**Completion evidence:** Every faithful transitive geometric generic-monodromy action of characteristic-zero polynomial Keller self-maps of ordinary affine space is decided by actual globally polynomial witnesses or absolute action obstructions, or by a necessary-and-sufficient criterion proved globally in both directions. A4 and natural degree12 PSL2(11) are now excluded; exceptional11 still needs an actual map or an absolute obstruction. A chart, allowable passport, rational field model or constructor-only theorem cannot complete the full spectrum.

Absolute affine inertia, stabilizer normal generation, regular/nilpotent action and central prime-cover obstructions are proved; A4 and natural PSL2(q), q3 modulo4, are excluded absolutely. Actual symmetric, alternating, signed, binary and marked-root wreath families and their precise actions/constants are retained. Independent-curve and rank2 normalized exceptional routes, dominant marked cofactor descents and other closed architectures must not be requeued. ## WORK-DC2-COCYCLE-TRANSPORT

**Construct a bounded full quantum carrier without cotangent normalization**

**Disposition:** archived-programme. **Kind:** research. **Compute class:** none.

**Next step:** Construct a finite projective generic rank-one full Long action with Gauss-regular generator images and the intended intrinsic classical Long shadow, or prove an all-degree obstruction to every such generic action. QVA1 makes the formal C-frame automatic: the saturated valuation ideal has a derivative-stable gcd normalization and is principal. QPG1 then constructs the integral finite carrier. Generic rank-one freeness gives integral freeness and a scalar bounded lift; nonfree generic projective classes retain the QMC1 matrix consequence. Valuations and residues are invariant under rational fractional frames, so do not search frames to change that shadow. A completed division comparison between regular full formal graphs has no spatial poles and promotes under the finite generic hypotheses. Finite generic generation is still essential: rational logarithmic full pairs with noninteger residue or higher poles fail admission. The interior charge-one initial ideal excludes Gauss-regular full actions in all degrees; the QPF1 moving-divisor model passes the formal test but has no constructed full right action. Preserve the QPG1 finite-jet full comparison reduction, QUR1 all-parameter single-normalization exclusion, QIR1 fixed-action lattice uniqueness and the QTC1/QGC1/index/spectral/arithmetic boundaries. Require the complete right action and its intended shadow. No spatial-degree, matrix-size, pole or parameter-order sweeps as a substitute for generic carrier existence.

**Completion evidence:** A common spatial bound for an actual compatible full lift is proved, or an all-degree horizontal nonmembership theorem closes a specified map or family. A chosen representative's growing degree, isolated finite jets, formal existence, or a fixed support residue is insufficient.

**Prerequisites and boundary:** Retain QFL1's unrestricted homotopy and QFL2's valuation and finite-type proofs. Use inverse-degree bounds only over fields or their stated reduced rings, never silently over nilpotent jet rings. Keep exact finite quantum coordinate changes separate from arbitrary formal gauges. A negative result for Long's map alone would not prove DC2. Conditional on the cited arithmetic nonlifting theorem, QFL3 already excludes all finite cotangent/Keller and arithmetic-compatible canonical-shear words for Long; do not launch a degree or word-length search in that class. QSO1 assumes scalar finite-order operators and a differential-constant commutator; unbounded formal coefficient series need not be algebraic over the generic coefficient field. QGM1 is failure of a chosen algebraization and has a good alternate model; it does not establish intrinsic nonalgebraizability. QEF1 distinguishes actual local nilpotence from nilpotence in every finite parameter jet. Its rank-one dual criterion assumes algebraic rank one and torsion-freeness; it does not establish a free frame or intrinsic effectivity from a formal dual section. Arbitrary finite quantum gauges change raw differential orders. The QGM1 generic boundary model is also simple by QEF1, so adding generic bimodule simplicity does not guarantee a nonzero algebraic left dual. QPF1 is a left-module degeneration in every Weyl rank, not an algebraic graph with a constructed right Weyl action. Its formal regular class has a good alternative model. A compatible filtered-frame theorem supplies freeness only after its filtration, graded flatness and special graded-frame hypotheses have been checked; preservation by the right actions and a Long-compatible bounded representative remain separate. QHI1 gives generic freeness from actual full right-symbol transversality; parameter descent is separate. Its charge-one exclusion has one Bernstein degree at most two and arbitrary partner degree, not all higher-degree pairs or all rank-two models. Algebraic fractional-realization invariance does not imply invariance across every formal gauge class. QCL1 concerns the full symplectic tuple, not only a canonical fiber pair or a determinant-one Keller map. Its scalar closure need not hold for Long's displayed symbols. All cubic symplectic maps have bounded quantizations, but no noninvertible cubic symplectic example is supplied; any such normalized example must have a quadratic layer. Cotangent lifting of a noninvertible homogeneous cubic Keller map has degree at least five. QCC1 is an obstruction for the specified D0 component, not an exclusion of every cubic representative or Long's corrected D. Its stable classical proof uses the full toric joint centralizer; its normal-order quantum family has a specified finite polynomial eigenspace and excludes no arbitrary ordering. Ordinary polynomial source coordinates and fiber shears are not automatically symplectic. QCR1 assumes an admitted full classical frame. Formal centralizer classification does not ensure completion of an arbitrary fixed quantum partial tuple. The normalized-D boundedness equivalence fixes R and the other quantum images; formal R-fixing may destroy a common spatial bound, and changes of S,T or polarization remain separate. The deformed-coordinate counterexample distinguishes h-adic closure from finite polynomial generation. QRP1 concerns the specified vertical derivations and fiber translations fixing x,y in the R centralizer. Its exceptional torsion has unbounded r-power order even though every fiber test vanishes. The criterion completely classifies admission for the specified h-small translations of an admitted Long triple; it does not classify arbitrary moving-position canonical transformations or all admissible quantum triples, nor bound input corrections from coefficientwise vanishing alone. QGR1 supplies a sharp bound on primitives once the corrections have a common bound. QGR1 classifies the complete bounded R-preserving centralizer group in rank two, not arbitrary unbounded formal gauges or changes moving R. Its positive primitive bound requires a uniformly bounded globally exact F. Every full finite endomorphism fixing R is a gradient automorphism, but Long's proposed Weyl map assigns R as its first generator image rather than fixing the observable R. This stabilizer result therefore does not rule out Long's bounded quantization, establish bounded reachability between all full lifts, or normalize every deformed first image. Generic irreducibility forbids bounded target normalization of the scalar-shifted first observable r+c(h), despite a bounded mate and formal normalization. A bounded source translation removes that scalar shift; any prospective normalization theorem must state whether it permits source as well as target changes. QNI1 supplies exact full countercontrols to universal bounded comparison in every rank at least three, with identity contact of arbitrary order and a fixed forward degree12. It gives DC_n=>P(n,N)=>JC_n and an equivalence to JC_n on the cotangent-rescaling subclass, not an equivalence P to DC_n or a rank-two counterexample. Bound both the forward canonical change and its inverse; the inverse-degree theorem over fields cannot be applied to all nilpotent jets. Completed graph equivalence and left freeness do not remove this inverse-bound gate. Its application uses exact R and common finite spatial support, not merely coefficientwise polynomial formal series. It forces S to increase order in that class; it does not exclude the increase or supply a bounded R normalization. Its full image-position statement allows a deformed first image if it stays positional, but not momentum terms. No source coordinate change recovers a two-position polarization in that chart. Its formal quantum corollary requires regular changes with regular inverses and invertible classical reductions. Intrinsic image Hamiltonian nilpotence is distinct from ambient nilpotence. The all-degree obstruction concerns a single position-preserving normal form, not every composition of multiple noninvertible cotangent maps. QEI1 bounds finite scalar pairs from their cubic energy, not arbitrary formal representatives. Formal fixed-energy flows show why finiteness is needed. Its source quantum centralizer and normalizer remain image-internal under an injective lift; additional ambient commuting operators are not classified. The fixed-energy flow controls do not rule out a theorem producing a different bounded pair with that energy; such an existence theorem remains a possible positive route. PBW growth proves both generic indices finite; equality of the indices uses the cited external index-symmetry preprint. The generic-minus-completed dimensions are stable under regular bounded canonical changes and identity padding, not arbitrary formal gauges. Its six-by-six matrices represent an elliptic curve operator algebra, not the whole matrix Weyl algebra or a Weyl endomorphism. Schur commutative centralizers and matrix trace exclude every finite-matrix realization sending its central b to a nonscalar scalar differential operator. A useful noncentral-energy bridge must change the algebra or reduction rather than use that forbidden substitution. QEM1 is a genuine energy-constrained obstruction with arbitrary rational poles and unbounded spatial degrees; it does not contradict QFL1 formal lifting, whose escape jet moves the energy transversely. Its h-adic energy-commutator order is distinct from QEI1 scalar differential order. Rational logarithmic normalizing gauges are formal and have no proved common spatial bound. The all-parity theorem is rational; only the normalized second-order nonexactness is asserted for arbitrary finite algebraic fiber covers. The flat Ore algebras and their diagonal central reduction are explicit, but a compatible deformation of the isogeny module is still absent. Preservation of a central character alone does not mean exact energy preservation, since the invariant derivation may also deform. Target changes moving the natural cubic and nonpositional R deformations are not excluded. Only the base and indices1,2 require finite exception checks; all later admission follows from R-power factors. The reference lift has no common spatial bound because [h^(2n)]S has degree8n-1. Fixed momentum orders and its quadratic energy do not violate QSO2 or QEI1 because the unbounded position series is not in the generic algebraic coefficient field. The finite-seed h6 relation replay is not the all-orders proof. No bounded comparison between this reference and all other full lifts is proved; formal Hamiltonian equivalence alone is insufficient by QNI1. Other formal representatives may still be bounded, so neither the PI divergence nor its finite canonical orbit closes Long or DC2. QFG1 extends QGR1 only to the finite-momentum formal category. Its full relative admission criterion remains coefficientwise and includes exceptional torsion. Formal target comparison is unique, but need not preserve any spatial or momentum bound. ## WORK-GMC3-PURE-PREFIX

**Least global ternary cubic pure prefix in[20,94]**

**Disposition:** archived-programme. **Kind:** research. **Compute class:** none.

**Next step:** Secondary under the explicit all-degree priority: retain least general/odd[20,94] and homogeneous[14,94] as open. Do not launch successive cutoff refinements or full coefficient radical rounds unless they decide a reusable universal lemma or unlock a new degree, dimension or architecture. I94 with at most7 monotone radical-search rounds remains the retained in-principle route. Both lower witnesses are complete; do not recreate either witness search. Equality of consecutive moment ideals is insufficient. Independent review remains useful; leastness,20/14 sufficiency and expanded I94 cofactors remain distinct.

**Completion evidence:** Exact least global K has complete sufficiency and verified insufficiency at K-1. General/odd/homogeneous94 upper bounds do not settle or equate least thresholds;expanded I94 cofactors remain separate assurance.

**Prerequisites and boundary:** Read RANK_ONE_TWO_BRANCH_GLOBAL94.md and retained rank-factor,conic,actual-seed and analytic proofs. Both quadratic roots and the missing restored direction are essential. Keep exact Jacobian and original phase/normalization derivatives;charge Hermite loss2 once per minor and divide in the joint-graded ring before constant-q specialization. Extend across merged roots polynomially and retain every lower-degree/parent/null branch. Preserve the initial rational-comparison failure and diagnostic.

## WORK-FACTORIAL-GENERAL

**Resolve general higher-dimensional FC/SFC after the completed binary FC/EIT and rigidity audits**

**Disposition:** archived-programme. **Kind:** research. **Compute class:** none.

**Next step:** OVERARCHING GOAL ACTIVE: resolve general Factorial and/or unrestricted Strong Factorial rigorously. Completed support families, whole cubic, all-gap n1..4 and gap3 n1..5 remain closed in their recorded scopes. Gap3 identities, coefficient positivity and one-real-section criterion are proved. NEW uniform polar companions have simple roots below-1 for all gamma>n-2, but generic inverse transfer to W sections is refuted. NEXT exploit the actual arithmetic progression gamma+2+3j to prove a valid transfer yielding some real-rooted section/constant-linear combination, or prove actual-family nonzero backward three-step pivots. Do not require positive pivots when nonzero suffices, and treat zero pivots as inconclusive or use a justified look-ahead method. Neither uniform gate is proved; finite positive certificates are not an all-index theorem. Do not apply an infinite zero-free-ray theorem to backwards sampling that has positive roots. Native prime3 repeated residuals at22 and surviving degree2 occupancy at63 rule out those shortcuts only. Preserve routes toward arbitrary lower exponents, genuinely multivariate supports and unrestricted FC/SFC; no reduction from completed special families to the full conjectures is established. Goal stays active and assurance flags false.

**Completion evidence:** The full arbitrary-polynomial Factorial and Strong Factorial questions have proofs or counterexamples, Long claims and bibliography have completed scoped reviews, and transfers are backed by original-marker certificates. The existing rigidity proof and special-family SFC alone do not complete the objective.

**Prerequisites and boundary:** Read the coupled-block proof and current source ledger. The block limit allows inactive variables and all positive real shapes; use active marker degree and unchanged inactive Gamma expectations. Complex-scale specialization requires fixed algebraic shapes. The arithmetic cube certificates require algebraic scales and marker coefficients. Functional E-independence and an ordinary nonzero point are both needed for Beukers lifting. Products of uniforms are a genuine coupled class, not every triangle phase. Zero leading marker periods do not prove whole zero sequences. Complex-scale FC uses algebraic specialization plus exact power closure; all-ring ordinary tail-unit ideals give existence of finite Bezout witnesses, not an effective universal cutoff or SFC window.
